name: Linked multi-view shape mirroring and class ids
answer: YES - in linked mode one linked operation makes ONE object, so it must carry the same class in both images. Legacy's split behaviour - polygons share a class id while boxes, circles and accepted AI masks each take their own viewer's active or next id - is an inconsistency with no rationale in the code, and decision 8 already settles how to treat it: multi-view is rebuilt as a synchronized split view from the linked-operation rules, and the half-migrated legacy path is deleted rather than ported. A rule that behaves three different ways depending on which tool drew the shape is exactly what 'rebuild from the rules' is for. SAYING 'THE SAME CLASS ID' IS NOT QUITE ENOUGH, AND THE GAP MATTERS. Decision 6 keeps class ids PER IMAGE, so the number 3 in one image's annotation file and the number 3 in another's are not the same class - each file carries its own alias table, and 'car' can be id 1 in one and id 2 in the next. Copying the numeric id across a linked pair therefore guarantees nothing on its own: it produces matching numbers that can mean different things, which is worse than a visible mismatch because every export looks consistent. THE INVARIANT IS THE NAME, AND THE ID FOLLOWS FROM IT. A linked operation resolves the active class to its ALIAS, then, in each image independently, uses the id that alias already has there, or allocates that image's next free id and records the alias against it. Both images then name the object the same thing, which is what a user means by 'the same class', and each file stays internally consistent with decision 6 and byte-identical to what legacy would have written for that image alone. Where the active class has no alias, the id is the name - legacy writes str(class_id) - so the two images must share the numeric id in that case, and allocating a different one would be the same bug in a different place. AN UNRESOLVED PART, DELIBERATELY LEFT TO PHASE 6 ENTRY. If the two images already disagree - 'car' is id 1 in the left and id 4 in the right - the rule above is still well defined and produces the right names. What it cannot do is keep ids equal as well, and nothing here should pretend otherwise. Decision 8 explicitly schedules the per-viewer class-id space as a Phase 6 entry decision, so the choice between 'names always agree, ids may differ' (what this answer specifies) and a stricter 'reconcile the id spaces on link' belongs there, with the split view in front of the approver. PRIORITY: not P0. The card's suspected defect is real, but it mislabels rather than destroys, and it is recoverable by reassignment. What Phase 5 owes this rule is that the linked-operation path resolves classes by alias rather than by id, so Phase 6 has one behaviour to extend instead of three to reconcile.
unresolved: Whether a linked pair whose images already assign different ids to the same alias should also have its ids reconciled, or only its names. Decision 8 schedules the per-viewer class-id space as a Phase 6 entry decision; this answer specifies name agreement, which is well defined either way.
corrections: Answered the open SME question: yes, a linked operation gives the same class in both images, and the per-tool inconsistency is a defect to delete rather than port.

Corrected what 'the same class id' can mean under decision 6: ids are per image, so copying the number produces matching values that may name different classes. The invariant is the alias; the id is resolved per image from it.
Named the one case where the numeric id must match after all - a class with no alias, where legacy writes str(class_id) and the id IS the name.
Recorded the genuinely open part as unresolved rather than deciding it here: reconciling two images that already disagree is the per-viewer class-id question decision 8 schedules for Phase 6 entry.
